messages.author: ed2ac94694ffb33f
messages.subject: Bifactor-model estimation method
parts:
Sorry, one more question:
As far as I understand mirt and bifactor models I could use the "bfactor" command or "mirt" command to estimate a bifactor model.
When I do so and compare model parameters e.g. with "bfactor" and "mirt" with the "MHRM"-method there are small but existing differences.

Would you say there is like a rule or a paper or something to lean on to decide which to choose?

Thank you very much in advance

Janine

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Bifactor-model estimation method
parts:
The MH-RM algorithm is nice to help with the general dimensionality problem, and you're right that mirt() should be close to bifactor() in this case. I think the problem is a computational time one mostly, because the MH-RM likely can take a lot longer with larger datasets. Also, if the number of factors is too high then controlling the Metropolise tuning parameters can be a little tricky, and requires a good amount of trial-and-error.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Bifactor-model estimation method
parts:
On Wed, Jan 31, 2018 at 5:48 PM, <janine.f...@gmail.com> wrote:
Also thank you very much for this answer. Would you say it is "safe to say": When in doubt just take the "bfactor" command - because it is especially suited for the bifactor-case and even faster?
Yes. And because computing the SEs and ACOV estimate (via the default "Oakes" identity approximation) is considerably more stable/accurate than via the stochastic MH-RM approach.
